chunks: Ahmad, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from his brother, from Dawud ibn al-Nu'man, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'I tested white slave-girls and black ones, and there was a disparity between them.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam mean by the disparity between white and black slave-girls?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates his empirical observation of 'white and black' slave-girls, noting a distinct disparity between them, which is frequently cited in Shia scholarly discourse regarding physical attributes, temperament, or spiritual potential. This report highlights the Imam’s practical engagement with the social realities of his time, using observable human differences to illustrate broader principles of distinction and merit.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad, from his father, from Ali Bin Al No’man, from his brother, from Dawood Bin Al Noman, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazaz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>  having said:
‘I<sup>asws</sup> put to test the white slave girls and black, and there was a disparity between the two’. (different qualities)
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad has narrated from his father from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from his brother from Dawud ibn al-Nu’man from abu Ayyub al- Khazzaz who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
I have put to the test white and dark color slave-girls. There is a great difference between them.’” (It may also mean both kinds are good)
